correctness.rationale: For every d>=2 and w in [0,1], the proof identifies exact target atomic masses and the norm via total variation. All possible component allocations of three maps give explicit lower bounds a=2w(d-1)/d and b=2(1-min(2/3,2w/d)). Both are attained by globally continuous maps constructed through one-fiber two-map and two-distinct-fiber three-map guarded lifts. The guarded triple move graph is connected by pair six-cycles and overlaps; finite graph edges support continuous transport. Exact comparison yields the stated piecewise law, including d=2 and endpoints. The packaged checker executed 4214 rational phase tests and guard-graph connectivity to d=9 as supplementary confirmation.

value.rationale: The first nontrivial budget after the existing two-map componentwise-cover classification gives an exact attained operator-norm invariant for every degree of connected covering and every component mass. It detects a universal transition w=d/(d+1) between use of an available global section and use of exclusively nontrivial moving atoms, with a sharp d=2 plateau. The mechanism is a structural transport lemma; it is not a benchmark-specific numerical increment or a parameter renaming.
